principles: Move config to match the authoritative intent, not the other way: three sources (handler guard, command-policy, B-804c) already agree on the 4-phase set; config is the lone outlier.
Never reduce a documented capability to satisfy a consistency check — narrowing would remove a real recovery path.
Keep the change minimal and literal (exact 'dev_start' entries), no behavior change, no wildcard widening.
Make the invariant mechanically enforced, not by convention (the existing contract check).
drivers: npm run test:process-fact-contract fails (exit 1) on dev_start INIT + DEV.
The dev_start handler REQUIRES INIT (atomic bootstrap) and permits DEV (manual recovery); config silently refuses a manual dev_start there via the phase-tools gate.
Two sources of truth for dev_start's phases disagree, with no guard catching future divergence until this story confirms the contract covers it.

options.name: Widen config to the 4-phase set (chosen)
pros: Aligns config with the handler's own allowedPhases guard AND command-policy AND the B-804c intent.
Restores the documented manual dev_start recovery in DEV (and INIT), which the phase-tools gate currently refuses.
Additive and literal — lowest blast radius; no behavior or other-command change.
cons: Permits a manual dev_start in INIT where there is no worktree yet — but the handler already allows/needs INIT and is idempotent, and owner-lease + scope-freeze gates still apply, so no new unsafe capability is introduced.

options.name: Narrow command-policy to INIT_CHECK + PLAN
pros: Also makes the two tables agree with a small edit.
cons: Contradicts the dev_start handler's own allowedPhases = ['INIT','INIT_CHECK','PLAN','DEV'] guard — the handler would still accept INIT/DEV while policy refuses them, a new inconsistency.
Removes the documented bootstrap/recovery window (INIT required by the atomic flow; DEV manual recovery) — a real capability regression.

rationale: The authoritative dev_start phase set is ['INIT','INIT_CHECK','PLAN','DEV'], independently asserted by the handler's own guard (worktree.ts:823, INIT required by the atomic bootstrap), by command-policy.ts, and by the B-804c reason. config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS is the only source with the narrower set and is the bug. Widening config restores the documented recovery capability and aligns all sources; narrowing command-policy would contradict the handler and remove capability, so it is rejected.

preMortem.scenario: Adding dev_start to INIT in DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS lets a user run a standalone dev_start in INIT and corrupt state.
preMortem.trigger: Manual lattice dev_start in INIT where no worktree exists yet.
preMortem.mitigation: No NEW capability is added: the handler already accepts INIT (it must, for the atomic flow) and is idempotent (re-bootstrap), and owner-lease + INIT scope-freeze gates still apply. The phase-tools gate was the only thing inconsistently blocking the manual path; aligning it matches the handler's existing contract. Confirm by reading the handler guard and running validate.

preMortem.scenario: The edit uses a wildcard or wrong pattern that widens OTHER commands' phase permissions.
preMortem.trigger: Adding a broad pattern (e.g. 'dev_*') instead of the literal 'dev_start' to the phase arrays.
preMortem.consequence: Unintended commands become allowed in INIT/DEV; the contract's reverse check may pass while real permissions drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Add only the exact literal 'dev_start'. Run npm run test:process-fact-contract (it asserts both directions: policy<->config per command, and every DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS pattern maps to a policy-approved command).

preMortem.scenario: Fixing dev_start uncovers OTHER pre-existing drifts so the contract still fails.
preMortem.trigger: assertCommandPolicyPhaseAlignment iterates ALL commands; other mismatches could exist.
preMortem.consequence: npm run test:process-fact-contract still exits 1 after the dev_start fix.
preMortem.mitigation: The observed failure listed ONLY dev_start INIT + DEV. Re-run the full contract after the fix; if a different command drifts, it is out of this story's scope (separate story) and must be called out, not silently bundled. The goal is the contract fully green with the dev_start fix being the only change.
